A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MACCA by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MPE and SMAC experiments, including benchmark comparisons, causal-graph ablations and ground-truth reward comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds training-order, threshold-sensitivity, non-additive-reward and reward-prediction experiments.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, reward substitution and alternating Algorithm 1 are retained. Section 4.3 replaces vaguely stated L1-norm-based zeroing with explicit elementwise binary thresholding. Because v1 already describes binary masks, the PDFs do not resolve whether this changes inference or clarifies its description.

E1.justification: The original MPE tasks and SMAC maps remain. v3 adds a sparse-reward MPE-CN scenario requiring all three agents to cover distinct landmarks jointly, extending evaluation to a non-additive success requirement within an existing environment.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. However, v3 removes the standalone OMAR backbone row from the causal-graph comparison in Table 6, although OMAR remains evaluated elsewhere. Newly cited related methods are not added as benchmark baselines.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark dataset categories, metrics and hyperparameter tables are retained. Added analyses introduce matched 10-million-step training-order controls, a five-value threshold sweep, and post-convergence per-agent MSE/MAE evaluation. These additions do not establish that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained regularization, ground-truth-reward and graph-type analyses, v3 tests alternating versus initial causal-model training, robustness to non-additive rewards, sensitivity to clipping threshold h, and individual-reward prediction accuracy across dataset qualities. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report means with plus/minus variability and retain the main-text statement of three SMAC seeds and the implementation appendix's general five-seed statement. The added tables extend existing reporting practices; no new confidence-interval, significance-testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores and retained ablation entries are unchanged. New results include training-order win rates of 0.62 versus 0.73 in Table 7 and sparse-reward returns of 0.18 for OMAR versus 0.42 for MACCA-OMAR in Table 8. Tables 12–14 add threshold, prediction-error and timing results. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance improvements between versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: Section 3 revises the Dec-POMDP transition and objective definitions and adds an explicit DBN temporal factorization. The identifiability proposition, Markov/faithfulness assumptions and proof remain substantively unchanged after appendix renumbering. Additive reward aggregation was already present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and main conclusion retain the same central claims: identifiable causal reward decomposition, interpretable credit assignment, compatibility with offline-learning backbones and improved offline MARL performance. Added experiments primarily support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of non-additive-reward applicability, alternating training, mask regularization and reward accuracy across dataset qualities. It revises the explanation of the ground-truth performance gap and explicitly discusses simulation-only validation and risks from biased offline data. These considerably expand the applicability boundaries and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds fixed-graph averaging details, wall-clock training times and an estimated 8–15% causal-model overhead. Architecture and hyperparameter disclosures remain largely unchanged. The new resource description in Appendix F.7 specifies three A30 GPUs and 500 GB memory, conflicting with the retained A100 and 5 TB description in F.3.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted comparisons with Zhang et al. (2024) on causal return decomposition and Hammond et al. (2023) on causality in games, plus citations supporting training-order interpretation. It removes several application-oriented references and corrects ICQ/CQL attribution while retaining the overall offline causal-credit-assignment positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, causal-RL discussion, preliminaries, method explanations and several ablation interpretations undergo substantial rewriting or expansion. Reproducibility moves from Section 7 to an appendix, and the appendix organization expands to accommodate broader impacts and additional implementation analyses.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a substantially different journal layout, author block and typography, relocates the workflow figure and multiple tables, and adds five tables. Table 1 reorders baseline columns and Table 6 changes its structure. Existing causal diagrams, heatmaps and environment illustrations are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: Added ablations, robustness testing and explicit limitations address useful gaps. However, the new reward-accuracy evidence is internally inconsistent: Table 13 reports Random MAE 4.45 while the prose says 2.45, and its MAE/MSE pairs violate the usual MAE-squared bound without explaining different scaling. Hardware disclosures also conflict. With the original benchmark results and proof retained, these benefits and new reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net quality improvement.
